clinicalPearls: Usually autosomal recessive growth hormone insensitivity, most often from growth hormone receptor (GHR) mutations, causing severe postnatal growth failure
The defining biochemistry is high or normal circulating growth hormone with low IGF-1 that fails to rise after growth hormone administration
Clinical features include proportionate short stature, frontal bossing, a depressed nasal bridge, small genitalia, and a high-pitched voice
Fasting hypoglycaemia is common in infancy because IGF-1 deficiency and altered fuel handling impair glucose maintenance
Because the defect lies downstream of growth hormone, growth hormone replacement is ineffective; recombinant IGF-1 is the specific treatment for growth and metabolic benefit
Populations with Laron syndrome show notably low rates of diabetes and cancer, illustrating the growth hormone/IGF-1 axis in growth and proliferation
It contrasts with isolated growth hormone deficiency, where growth hormone itself is low and replacement works
Diagnosis rests on the growth pattern, the high-GH/low-IGF-1 profile with a failed IGF-1 generation test, and GHR genetics
reference.pathophysiology: Laron syndrome is a state of growth hormone insensitivity in which growth hormone is secreted normally or in excess but cannot act, most commonly because of loss-of-function mutations in the growth hormone receptor (GHR). Growth hormone normally binds its hepatic receptor to stimulate IGF-1 production, which mediates most of its growth-promoting effects; when the receptor is defective, IGF-1 generation fails despite high growth hormone levels. The resulting profound IGF-1 deficiency produces severe postnatal growth failure and characteristic craniofacial features, while loss of IGF-1's metabolic actions contributes to fasting hypoglycaemia in early life. Because the block is at or beyond the receptor, only IGF-1 replacement, not growth hormone, restores signalling.
additionalDifferentials: IGF-1 gene or IGF-1 receptor defects
Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
Other skeletal dysplasias or syndromic short stature
additionalInvestigations: Basal growth hormone (high or normal) and IGF-1 (low)
IGF-1 generation test, which fails to raise IGF-1 after growth hormone
IGF binding protein-3 and acid-labile subunit levels
GHR gene sequencing and testing of downstream signalling genes where indicated
Fasting glucose monitoring for hypoglycaemia in infants
Bone age and growth velocity assessment
redFlags: Recurrent fasting or nocturnal hypoglycaemia in infancy
Severe growth failure crossing centiles downward
Signs of hypoglycaemic seizure or encephalopathy
Marked developmental or feeding difficulties in an affected infant
reference.prognosis: Untreated individuals have marked short stature but often a favourable metabolic profile with low rates of diabetes and malignancy; recombinant IGF-1 improves growth, though final height usually remains below average.
pitfalls: Giving growth hormone replacement, which fails because the defect is downstream
Misdiagnosing the condition as isolated growth hormone deficiency without checking IGF-1 response
Overlooking infantile hypoglycaemia as a presenting feature
Ignoring the diagnostic value of the IGF-1 generation test
Failing to distinguish GHR defects from IGF-1 or IGF-1-receptor defects
references: Endocrine Society clinical practice guidance on growth disorders
management: Give the specific treatment - recombinant human IGF-1 (mecasermin) - since growth hormone replacement is ineffective when the block lies at or beyond its receptor
Prevent and treat fasting hypoglycaemia, especially in infancy, with regular feeding and by giving IGF-1 together with food, as the therapy itself can cause hypoglycaemia
Monitor growth velocity and bone age and watch for IGF-1 treatment effects such as lymphoid and tonsillar hypertrophy, raised intracranial pressure and slipped capital femoral epiphysis
Coordinate multidisciplinary care through paediatric endocrinology, dietetics and auxology
Provide psychosocial support for the effects of short stature
Offer genetic counselling and family testing given the usually autosomal recessive inheritance
